82557bfe: Optimum makes blockchain data move faster between the machines that run a network. Its first product, mump2p, gets each new Ethereum block to validators sooner than the default route does.
301f24a5: It does not change Ethereum itself. Operators run a small extra program next to their node, and blocks start arriving earlier.
3bfe56a3: Why a few hundred milliseconds matter
497f6fa1: Ethereum makes a block every 12 seconds, and validators have to vote on it quickly. A validator that sees the block late can miss the vote or vote on the wrong thing, and that costs rewards. Across a market of staked ETH worth around 100 billion dollars, small delays add up.
693d92a4: That is the idea behind the slogan the team uses: speed is money.
4b9a8c53: How it works, without the math
a56222b0: Normally a block travels as a whole, passed from peer to peer, and every peer waits for the full copy before sending it on.
899d4cdf: mump2p cuts the block into pieces and mixes them into coded pieces with a technique called Random Linear Network Coding (RLNC). Think of each coded piece as one equation about the block: once a node holds enough independent equations, from any senders in any order, it can solve for the whole block. Nodes in the middle can also mix fresh pieces from what they already hold, without waiting for the full block.
fafbdf32: An operator runs a gateway: one container on a host next to the beacon node. The gateway acts as a peer of the consensus client and never receives validator keys. Prysm, Lighthouse, Teku, Nimbus and Lodestar are supported, and the usual gossip route keeps running alongside it, so the gateway adds a faster path instead of replacing one.
facb448f: People without validators can run a stream only gateway to receive the block stream.
e6f4c561: Signal hands blocks from the Optimum mesh to your beacon node so your validators receive them sooner. It is free for Ethereum validators.
c78a06ce: Accelerate goes further for large operators: it recommends a bid cutoff for the MEV sidecar they already run, based on the slots their validators proposed. It needs at least 200 active mainnet validators and has to be enabled by Optimum.
8d647848: Flexnodes are extra nodes that add bandwidth and shorten distances in the network. They receive block data through a gateway and send more coded pieces to the validators that need them. Operators would be paid through a Latency Marketplace, where validators pay for the pieces they need.
afb36512: The early rollout is limited to existing validator partners, with wider community participation planned after testing.
2a77e6fe: What the evidence says so far
0bf4fda8: Optimum's own figures, published live on its Hub, show blocks reaching nodes faster than the default gossip route in most slots. Outside checks are more mixed: a Lido evaluation on the Hoodi testnet found blocks arriving about 407 ms sooner at the 95th percentile, while an independent StereumLabs test on 36 mainnet nodes with an early gateway build found some clients faster and none statistically significant.

7598d52e: A DefiLlama Research spotlight published on 19 November follows the money from attesters to proposers. Citing Optimum's Impact Report, it says wrong head votes fell 34.3% on average across operators, and that in six MEV-Boost experiments blocks could go out about 160 ms later with no rise in orphaned blocks, which Optimum models as an 8.4% bid uplift. 632f8543: 93% of blocks now arrive faster, up from 88% at launch
f81811c7: On 17 November Optimum said mump2p holds a reliable latency advantage of more than 200 ms and that 93% of blocks arrive faster, up from 88% on launch day. This week's Hub report puts the share of slots seen first on mump2p at 92.5%. Co-founder Kent Lin added on 18 November that he expects 10% of Ethereum stake on mump2p by the end of the year.
cbb9b18f: Outside tests: one clear gain, one inconclusive
dada9a6d: A Lido evaluation on the Hoodi testnet (17 September to 15 October, 180,327 slots) measured a 95th percentile arrival of 1,207 ms at mump2p gateways against 1,614 ms at public reference nodes, a 407 ms difference. It compares two groups rather than paired deliveries, and testnet is not mainnet. An earlier independent StereumLabs test on 36 mainnet nodes, using an early gateway build and no attached validators, saw earlier arrivals on some clients but nothing statistically significant.

fd43f468: In a 9 November post about Ethereum's roadmap, Vitalik Buterin listed erasure coded peer to peer networking for large data objects as a useful improvement, with implementation complexity as the main tradeoff. He did not name Optimum, and his proposals are separate from mump2p, but it is the same family of ideas.
